A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Frozen-PINN work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original PDE simulations, training times, approximation errors, and ablation results in Section 3, Table 1, and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds wave-equation and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky simulations, sensitivity studies, and deeper-PINN experiments.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithm 1 retain the frozen ELM/SWIM features, time-dependent output coefficients, least-squares initialization, adaptive ODE integration, two boundary treatments, and SVD compression. Adaptive resampling and directional projection already appear in v2. The new PDE experiments apply existing components.

E1.justification: v3 adds wave propagation with two-frequency and three-frequency initial conditions, testing multiscale solutions, and the chaotic Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation (Sections 3.3 and 3.6; Appendices C.3 and C.7). These substantially extend the physical and solution-complexity coverage. The earlier benchmark settings remain represented.

E2.justification: The new wave comparison in Table 1 introduces FBPINN, gPINN, and NTK-based PINN results from Hao et al. (2024), alongside L-BFGS PINN. The Burgers comparison removes Urbán et al. (2025)'s PINN (BFGS) row while retaining their SSBroyden row. The remaining comparator sets are preserved.

E3.justification: New protocols include 10- and 20-layer PINNs trained for 20,000 epochs under different learning rates, controlled numerical-parameter sweeps, and qualitative pattern assessment for chaotic dynamics. Section 2.4 changes the reported default boundary penalty from 1000 to 100000; Table 4 changes the reported Frozen-PINN layer count from 2+3i to 2. These reported revisions do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds initial-condition fitting sensitivity via rcond (Figure 9), SVD-cutoff sensitivity across three PDEs (Figure 10), and boundary-penalty sensitivity for Euler-Bernoulli (Figure 15). Tables 6–7 additionally examine PINN depth, optimizer, and learning-rate effects. These test substantial new questions beyond v2's retained width, sampling, and SVD-presence ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the general three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting protocol. v3 specifically reports averaging the new Kuramoto-Sivashinsky runtimes over five seeds, without accompanying dispersion estimates. This adds experiment-specific run information; it does not demonstrate increased repetition of existing experiments.

E6.justification: New results include a wave error of 1.81e-6 ± 1.01e-6 in 0.56 seconds, three-frequency wave error below 1e-5, and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky runtimes of 2.7 and 6.9 seconds for different horizons. New sensitivity and deep-PINN results further expand the evidence; matched retained scores are largely unchanged. The wave result's variant is inconsistent: Table 1 labels it ELM, whereas Appendix C.3 identifies SWIM.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2.3 adds explicit wave and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky PDE-to-ODE derivations using the existing ansatz; prior mathematics is retained. The new wave derivation contains a sign error: u_tt - kappa u_xx = f requires a positive kappa spatial term on the right-hand side, but the displayed coefficient equations use a negative term.

C1.justification: The conclusion newly qualifies accuracy parity with mesh-based solvers as applying within the empirical study's scope. The abstract and introduction update the advertised benchmark count from eight to nine. The four principal contributions and central claims about speed, accuracy, temporal causality, and compression otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2.1 substantially expands interpretation of initial-fit error propagation, SVD accuracy-versus-stiffness tradeoffs, and boundary-strategy applicability. v3 also explains its qualitative treatment of chaotic trajectories and interprets deeper-PINN optimization behavior. The new assertion of failures across beta=40 configurations overstates Table 7, which includes a relative error of 4.37e-3.

D1.justification: v3 specifies float64 arithmetic, np.linalg.lstsq/rcond handling, and boundary-condition strategies in existing hyperparameter tables. It supplies architecture details for the added PDE experiments and announces an additional refactored repository intended for maintenance. These extend v2's already extensive implementation information; newly disclosed choices do not establish procedural changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hao et al. (2024)'s benchmark reference and an Appendix A paragraph discussing PINNsFormer and PINNMamba, citing Zhao et al. (2024) and Xu et al. (2025). It contrasts their sequence-modeling architectures and computational costs with Frozen-PINNs. The broader positioning and existing references remain intact.

P1.justification: v3 adds two empirical subsections and focused explanatory passages, updates the publication header and author affiliations, and compacts the author block. Most existing introduction, method, experimental narrative, and overall section organization are retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: The visual evidence substantially expands through new sensitivity plots, wave solution/error visualizations, a multiscale surface plot, chaotic-pattern comparisons, and deep-PINN tables. The PDE overview and Table 1 gain new benchmark content, and hyperparameter tables gain boundary-strategy rows. Existing displays are mostly retained and relocated, including the high-dimensional figure and Table 2.

improvement.justification: The new sensitivity studies make previously untested numerical dependencies assessable, while explicit boundary strategies and precision details reduce reproduction ambiguity. These provide a limited net gain over v2's already extensive evaluation. However, the new wave material has inconsistent ELM/SWIM labeling and an incorrect derivation sign, and Appendix C.1 overstates failures relative to Table 7. These issues limit the overall improvement.
